total Settled #

Lower bounds / separations — there is a family achieving this

  • \(\sqrt{\mathrm{s}(f)} \le \lambda(f)\)
    witness: \(\mathrm{AND}_n\) ABKRT21
    A star $K_{1,\mathrm{s}}$ sits inside the sensitivity graph, and $\lambda(K_{1,k})=\sqrt k$. Tight for AND: $\lambda(\wedge_n)=\sqrt n$, $\mathrm{s}(\wedge_n)=n$.
  • \(\lambda(\mathrm{PARITY}_n) = \mathrm{s}(\mathrm{PARITY}_n) = n\)
    witness: \(\oplus_n\) ABKRT21
    The other end of $\sqrt{\mathrm{s}} \le \lambda \le \mathrm{s}$: the sensitivity graph of $\oplus_n$ is the whole hypercube $Q_n$, which is $n$-regular, so $\lambda = n = \mathrm{s}$.

So $\sqrt{\mathrm{s}} \le \lambda \le \mathrm{s}$, and both ends are achieved. Huang''s theorem is the statement $\deg\le\mathrm{s}^2$; its spectral strengthening $\deg\le\lambda^2$ [ABKRT21, Thm 1] is what makes $\lambda$ worth its own column.

see also: \(\lambda(f)\), \(\mathrm{s}(f)\), \(\deg(f)\), [Huang19] data/relations/03-quantum.yaml

up.note: Spectral sensitivity is a quantum lower bound because $\lambda(f)\le\mathrm{Adv}(f)\le \mathrm{Adv}^{\pm}(f)=\Theta(\mathrm{Q}(f))$. Every link of that chain holds for partial $f$ -- the sensitivity graph is built from the domain edges, the eigenvector is a feasible adversary matrix, and $\mathrm{Adv}^\pm$ characterises $\mathrm{Q}$ off-promise too [LMRSS11] -- so the bound belongs here.

facts: $\lambda(f) \le \mathrm{Adv}(f) = O(\mathrm{Q}(f))$, so $\lambda$ lower-bounds quantum query complexity.

2026: $\mathrm{bs}(f)$ can exceed $\lambda(f)^2$ -- there is a total $f$ with $\mathrm{bs}(f)\ge\lambda(f)^{2.127}$ [Meiburg26], refuting an ABKRT question. Best upper bound remains $\mathrm{bs} = O(\lambda^4)$.
The single-bit private-coin certificate game value equals $\lambda(f)^2$ [CGLMSG23].

On a promise $\lambda$ is not weak but empty: if no two promise inputs are adjacent the sensitivity graph has no edges at all, so $\lambda = 0$ while $\mathrm{D} = \Theta(n)$ (\(\mathrm{forr}\), \(\mathrm{GapMaj}^{\delta}_{n}\)). The collapse is sharper than for $\mathrm{Adv}$, which merely drops to $\Theta(1)$ there: an exact $0$ kills every candidate bound $M \le g(\lambda)$ at once, since it would read $M \le g(0)$.
self.name: Spectral sensitivity
self.short: Largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix of the sensitivity graph of f.

A single character has sparsity $1$ and $\mathrm{osss} = 1$: the two agree, but neither
grows, so this witnesses no exponent. No function in the zoo has $\mathrm{osss}$ growing
while $\mathrm{spar}$ stays bounded -- indeed $\mathrm{spar}(f) = O(1)$ forces $f$ to be a
constant-size combination of characters, and $\mathrm{osss}$ is then bounded too.
